sentences.sentence: An encyclopedia is a reference work that arranges articles so a reader can look up a subject without reading the whole book.
Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only world known to host liquid water and life at the surface.
The Sun is a G-type main-sequence star that fuses hydrogen into helium and supplies nearly all energy used by Earth's climate and biosphere.
The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite; its gravity raises tides and stabilizes the planet's axial tilt.
Water is the chemical compound H2O and the principal solvent of terrestrial life.
Air is the mixture of gases that forms Earth's atmosphere, mostly nitrogen and oxygen.
An atom is the smallest unit of an element that still has that element's chemical identity.
A molecule is a group of two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds.
A cell is the smallest living unit that can grow, copy its genome, and keep a membrane boundary.
DNA is the polymer that stores genetic instructions as a sequence of four bases.
Evolution is change in heritable traits of a population across generations, driven mainly by variation and natural selection.
Gravity is the attractive force between masses; near Earth it gives weight and holds the atmosphere.
Light is electromagnetic radiation in the band the human eye can detect, carried by photons.
Energy is the capacity to do work or heat a system; it is conserved in isolated physics.
Time is the ordered sequence in which events occur; clocks measure intervals against a chosen standard.
A number is an abstract object used to count, order, and measure quantity.
Zero is the integer that marks an empty count and enables place-value notation.
Geometry is the study of shape, size, and relative position in space.
A map is a scaled drawing of part of Earth or another surface, using a chosen projection.
An ocean is a vast body of salt water that covers most of Earth's surface.
A continent is a large continuous landmass, usually sitting on continental crust.
A mountain is high ground raised by crustal motion, volcanism, or erosion of surrounding rock.
A river is a natural freshwater channel that flows downhill toward a sea, lake, or another river.
Climate is the long-term average of weather in a region, including extremes.
Weather is the short-term state of the atmosphere at a place: heat, wind, cloud, and rain.
A plant is a living organism that typically makes food by photosynthesis using sunlight.
An animal is a multicellular organism that typically moves, ingests food, and lacks cell walls.
A human is a bipedal primate of the species Homo sapiens, marked by language and cumulative culture.
Language is a structured system of words and grammar used to share meaning.
Writing is a set of lasting marks that record speech or thought so it can be read later.
A place-value number system writes quantities as digits whose position multiplies a base, commonly base {n}.
A computer is a machine that stores data and follows a program of instructions.
An algorithm is a finite list of well-defined steps that turns an input into an output.
The internet is a global system of packet-switched networks that share a common addressing scheme.
Electricity is the set of effects produced by electric charge, including current in a wire.
A magnet is a body that produces a magnetic field and attracts iron near its poles.
Sound is a pressure wave in air or another medium that the ear can detect.
Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference; temperature tracks average molecular motion.
A metal is an element or alloy that is typically shiny, conductive, and malleable.
Stone is hard mineral matter; rock is a naturally occurring solid made of minerals or mineraloids.
Fire is rapid combustion that releases heat and light while consuming fuel and oxygen.
A year is the time Earth takes to complete one orbit of the Sun.
A day is the time Earth takes to rotate once relative to the Sun.
History is the study of the human past from records, remains, and testimony.
Law is a body of rules a political community treats as binding and enforceable.
Money is a widely accepted medium of exchange and a unit for recording value.
A city is a dense, lasting settlement that houses many people and specialized work.
A farm is land and practice used to raise food, fiber, or livestock.
Medicine is the craft of preventing, diagnosing, and treating disease in living bodies.
Music is organized sound in time, using tone, rhythm, and silence.
